title: Regular sequences on a module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-module. A finite sequence $f_1,\dots,f_r$ of elements of $R$ is an *$M$-regular sequence* if (1) for each $i=1,\dots,r$ the element $f_i$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M/(f_1,\dots,f_{i-1})M$ (multiplication by $f_i$ on this module is injective), and (2) $M/(f_1,\dots,f_r)M\neq0$. If $I\subset R$ is an ideal and all $f_i\in I$ it is an $M$-regular sequence in $I$; for $M=R$ it is called a *regular sequence* (in $I$).
